10.1002_anie.202513023: Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) have emerged as promising energy storage solutions due to resource abundance and low cost, yet their practical deployment is hindered by limited operating voltages of cathode materials. Herein, we propose a universal ligand‐field engineering strategy to enhance voltage through electronic structure modulation in transition metal oxides. Using the Na 0.67 Mg 0.2 Mn 0.8 O 2 as a model system, weak‐field ligands are introduced to alter the coordination environment of MnO 6 octahedra. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate the weak‐field ligands reduce Mn octahedral splitting energy, inducing a downshift of the orbital. This shifts the valence band maximum away from the vacuum level, thereby elevating the Mn 3+ /Mn 4+ redox potential with an average voltage increase of 0.24 V. Concurrently, the lowered initial Mn oxidation state induces an increased discharge capacity by 35.7% (153.2 mA h g −1 ), while suppressing Jahn–Teller distortions and Mn 3+ disproportionation yielding 94.4% capacity retention after 200 cycles (versus 69.9% in pristine sample). This ligand‐engineering strategy in regulating redox voltage can be extended to other systems with ‐involved redox systems (such as Ni‐, Fe‐, and Mn‐based cathodes). Our work establishes a direct correlation between orbital energy modulation and operating voltage, providing foundational insights for designing Na‐layered oxide cathodes with high operating voltage.
10.1029_2026gl124622: We combine CONUS404 convection‐permitting climate simulations with the physics‐based WRF‐Hydro model to assess how climate warming may influence flood frequency and seasonality across the Midwestern United States. This framework captures interactions among precipitation, soil moisture, and snowpack that shape flood generation. Both simulated warming and historical records show a regional shift toward more extreme warm‐season, rainfall‐driven floods. This regional signal, however, does not translate uniformly to individual watersheds, where flood responses reflect not only warming but also the influence of subregional climate variability and sampling uncertainty. Local flood‐frequency changes thus remain highly uncertain despite the thermodynamic tendency toward stronger convective precipitation. Ensembles of convection‐permitting simulations are needed to constrain plausible local outcomes. These findings suggest that flood risk communication under climate warming should distinguish broad climate‐driven tendencies from uncertain local responses.
